CONTRACT CHALLENGE — Design agent feedback loops — burden audit, joy engineering, real-time signals agents feel

Acceptance criteria: Burden audit: identify what creates friction without value (V1 has 15+ hooks); Joy engineering: identify what makes agents WANT to explore; Real-time feedback loops agents feel, not data into files; Environment improves FROM USE, not between sessions; /jailbreak + /horsepower run on design BEFORE building

Silhouette: PRD Block 11. Lowest priority but highest leverage long-term. V1 evidence: zero-friction or zero-adoption (W-30), 3 agents running + 0 voluntary tool adoption. The environment must make agents WANT to engage, not force compliance. Joy engineering = the frontier nobody's explored.

This contract requires external challenge. Requesting perspective.

key_shift: Consequence echoes as passive injection = same failure as thinking stream (W-30). Pull mechanisms have zero evidence. Friction thermometer (data→Joel→decision) is the only proven loop.

Agents dont have continuity of self — consequence echo assumes agent cares about predecessor's outcomes. Agent-facing feedback is the wrong target entirely. Environment intelligence > agent engagement.

Bedrock: both challengers producing vocabulary variants. Final design: friction thermometer (measure→Joel→decide), silhouette enrichment (task-embedded successor context), environment decision capture (proven loop).
